passages.provision_quote: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
passages.note: Bill text of AB 1482 (2019-2020), the statewide rent-cap/just-cause bill Ramos voted No on (see vote page).
Assembly floor concurrence vote; Ramos listed among the Noes.

rows.reasoning: Ramos voted No on AB 1482 (2019-2020), a single-subject bill capping annual rent increases statewide at 5% plus CPI or 10% (whichever is lower) and requiring just cause for eviction. The No vote shows opposition to strengthening and extending rent stabilization, but on its own it does not separate which less-regulatory rung (market rents for new construction, subsidized-only regulation, or no rent control at all) he holds.
needs_source: A statement or later record from Ramos tying his No vote to a specific clause, or distinguishing among rungs 3-5
